Lead validation step: its card on the canvas (#2590)

The card the lead validation step shows on the canvas, the step that replaces each partner workflow's validate_bidding_and_state script (#934). For whoever reads or builds a partner workflow. Settled by Dan on 2026-10-21 in rounds 5 and 6 of six, drawn on the real canvas in place of a Filter card, at its width, beside Code, Branch and Data Store cards. The step's settings panel is settled in lead-validation-node.html beside this file.

The settled design. Every frame is drawn inside the product's real chrome, captured from https://bidspoke.trypennie.dev/workflows/0630d714-5917-4221-9bcc-ca1fb2d9eba2 (Main Flow (v2), switched off) in view mode, zoomed to 125% on its Filter card, Dan's signed in Chrome, 2026-10-21, from the committed fixture the built page renders too. The build is done when it scores 100% against this file on both halves.

Requirements

  • 2590 The lead validation step is on the canvas: a palette entry, a card, and a settings panel holding the lead id field and an ordered list of checks, each edited with the rule builder, a reason from LEAD_REJECTION_REASONS and what happens when the lead has no value.

Decisions

  1. C1 Under its title and step ID, the card says how many checks the step runs, "7 checks", and nothing more about them; the details live in the panel. Round 5: Dan chose "How many checks" over the first check names, and over the reasons it can give. Requirement 2590. Checked on card: The card headed "Lead validation" reads, below its header, these three lines first and in order: "Validate bidding and state", "validate_bidding_and_state" and "7 checks".
  2. C2 The card's header is slate: Tailwind slate 50 (#f8fafc) behind, slate 100 (#f1f5f9) for the rule under it, slate 700 (#334155) for the label, the same three steps every other card's header uses. Round 6: Dan chose Slate over Fuchsia, Yellow and Sky, a quiet grey blue that reads as a gate rather than an action and is distinct from Parallel's beige (9.9 to 1 contrast). Requirement 2590. Checked on card: The header holding "Lead validation" has background #f8fafc and a bottom border of #f1f5f9, and the "Lead validation" label is #334155.
  3. C3 The card has one way out, labelled pass, as a Filter card's pass: a rejected lead is answered by the step itself and goes nowhere else on the canvas. Held identical in rounds 5 and 6. Requirement 2590. Checked on card: After those three lines, the card's only text is "↓ pass": it names no other way out.

Exceptions Dan approved

None. A deliberate difference from this design is a new design round, or an exception Dan approves in his own words, recorded here.

Frames

Idioms of the medium, to translate rather than copy

  • The card is drawn in place of the Filter card in a captured copy of the canvas at 1120 wide, moved to the middle of the narrower pane; the canvas and every other card around it are the product as it is today, not decisions.
  • The card's icon is a checked box drawn inline; the build uses the matching lucide icon.
